text:
incident-bot: SEV1 alert — sudden spike in 5xx and timeouts observed on /v1/generate and /v1/stream endpoints in us-east-1 and eu-central. Auto-page sent to oncall.

erin (oncall-sre): I'm on the page. Seeing p95/p99 shoot up right after the 10:42 deploy. Beginning triage — posting initial observations.

jas (eng-runtime): pulling metrics. Was there a config change or a runtime bump in that deploy?

erin (oncall-sre): Deploy event: runtime canary (rev e7a4f2) promoted to 100% at 10:42 after canary passed basic checks. No model changes reported.

tom (eng-frontend): Alerts from customers: intermittent 502/504 on generate calls, streaming sessions drop mid-output. Example from support ticket:
```
POST /v1/stream
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Connection: close
```

jas (eng-runtime): Correlating logs: pod-level traces show increased request queueing and long goroutine stacks around KV cache eviction. Heap growth and frequent STW traces. p99 jumping from ~300ms -> ~5.6s. 5xx ratio from 0.2% -> 9% over ~10 minutes.

erin (oncall-sre): Initiating quick mitigations: 1) reduce traffic to new revision to 0%; 2) scale stable fleet +4; 3) enable temporary circuit-breaker on streaming route. Executing commands.

ops-rotation: @mira heads-up for customer comms.

mira (customer-ops): drafting a brief: "We've detected service degradation affecting generation and streaming. Engineering is rolling back the last runtime change and we'll update within 15 minutes." Will post after confirmation.

pagerduty-bot: rollback playbook suggested due to sustained p99 > 1s and 5xx > 1% for >5m.

jas (eng-runtime): Running replay tests against the canary image under bursty load — reproduces GC stalls and connection resets. Heap snapshots show many short-lived allocations pinned to cache refill path. New eviction heuristic in e7a4f2 appears to aggressively prefetch/pin large KV slices under heavy concurrency which spikes memory pressure.

erin (oncall-sre): Because customers are impacted and we can reproduce, I'm authorizing immediate rollback to revision 287 (previous stable). Rolling back now.

commands run:
```
# rollback to stable
redwoodctl deploy revert --service inference-runtime --revision 287 --env prod
kubectl rollout status deployment/inference-runtime -n prod
```

tom (eng-frontend): We can flip a header switch for new clients to hit `/v1/generate-stable` to reduce errors during the rollout. Enabling now for new sessions only.

jas (eng-runtime): Observing pod terminations and new pods coming up with revision 287. Readiness probes passing.

erin (oncall-sre): Watching SLOs: 5xx trending down: 9% -> 3.4% -> 0.9% within ~8 minutes. p95/p99 returning towards baseline.

mira (customer-ops): Posted interim update: rollback initiated; service restoration in progress; ticket updates will follow.

ops-rotation: Rollback completed at 10:53:12. Active revision confirmed: 287.

erin (oncall-sre): Post-rollback checks: p95 150ms, p99 420ms, 5xx 0.4%. Verified by synthetic smoke tests and customer ticket samples. Marking incident as mitigated.

jas (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: e7a4f2 introduced an adaptive prefetch and eviction behavior for KV cache that under bursty traffic pre-allocates large segments and triggers lock contention + GC thrash. Reproducible in load tests. Plan: revert change in repo, add targeted telemetry (evict/hit ratio, prefetch sizes, mem pressure), add a conservative backoff, and run stress tests.

erin (oncall-sre): Post-incident tasks: 1) jas to produce RCA and a patch for safe defaults; 2) erin to update canary policy: stricter p99/5xx gating and automatic rollback if thresholds breached; 3) mira to send a final customer summary and SLO remediation plan. I'll keep the incident open for 2 hours for monitoring and then schedule a 48h postmortem.

mira (customer-ops): Will include list of impacted tenants and suggested SLO credits in the follow-up.

ops-rotation: Handoff to jas for continued monitoring — erin's shift ends at 11:30.

erin (oncall-sre): Thanks team — incident mitigated, rolling into postmortem. Closing the active alert channel but leaving ticket open: INC-20260328-04.

incident-bot: Incident closed by erin (oncall-sre). Duration: 00:26:46. Follow-up: RCA + postmortem scheduled.
